essays.task: Az egyéni munka mellett gyakran dolgozunk csoportokban is. Fejtsd ki a véleményedet a csoportmunkáról, írj 2-2 érvet mellette és ellene!

essays.title: Kellenek-e nyomtatott tankönyvek?
essays.task: Szükség van-e ma a felső tagozaton nyomtatott tankönyvekre? Fejtsd ki a véleményedet érvekkel, és írd le, neked szükséged van-e rájuk!

essays.title: Hosszabb tanév, több szünet?
essays.task: Több európai országban hosszabb a tanév, de többször van szünet. Írj 2-2 érvet mindkét rendszerről, és fejtsd ki, számodra melyik előnyösebb!

essays.title: Csapatsport vagy egyéni sport?
essays.task: Van, aki a csapatsportokat, más az egyéni sportágakat kedveli. Írj 2-2 érvet mindkettő mellett, és fejtsd ki, te melyiket választanád és miért!

essays.title: Iskola vagy távoktatás?
essays.task: Írj 2-2 érvet a távoktatás mellett és ellen, és térj ki arra is, hogy neked inkább előnyt vagy hátrányt jelentene!

essays.title: Mozi vagy otthoni filmnézés?
essays.task: Van, aki moziba jár szívesen, más otthon néz filmet. Írj 2-2 érvet mindkét lehetőség mellett, és fejtsd ki, te melyiket választod!

essays.title: Szóbeli vagy írásbeli számonkérés?
essays.task: Van, aki szívesebben felel szóban, más inkább írásban ad számot a tudásáról. Írj 2-2 érvet mindkettő mellett, és fejtsd ki, neked melyik a jobb!

essays.title: Felnőttnek vagy gyereknek lenni jobb?
essays.task: Egyesek szerint felnőttnek lenni jobb, mások szerint gyereknek. Írj 2-2 érvet mindkét állítás mellett, és fejtsd ki a saját véleményedet!

essays.title: Kellenek-e tehetségkutató műsorok?
essays.task: Sok tehetségkutató műsor fut a tévében. Szükség van arra, hogy így bizonyítsák tehetségüket a fiatalok? Írj 2-2 érvet mellette és ellene!

essays.title: Iskolai egyenruha
essays.task: Van, ahol kötelező az egyenruha, máshol nincs ilyen szabály. Írj 2-2 érvet a kötelező egyenruha mellett és ellen, és fejtsd ki a véleményedet!

essays.title: Melyik szünidei programot javasolnád?
essays.task: Kirándulás, iskolai tábor vagy családi utazás? Válassz egy programot, és mutasd be az előnyeit és a hátrányait!

essays.title: Közösségi oldalak: mellette vagy ellene?
essays.task: Sokan használnak közösségi oldalakat, mások ellenzik őket. Írj 2-2 érvet a használatuk mellett és ellen, és fejtsd ki a véleményedet!

e2025-2: A nyári szünet a tanév legjobban várt időszaka, és sokat gondolkodom azon, hogyan érdemes eltölteni. Vannak, akik a táborokat szeretik, mások inkább a családjukkal pihennek.

A tábor mellett szól, hogy új barátokat szerezhetünk, és megtanulunk önállóan boldogulni a szüleink nélkül. Tavaly egy úszótáborban voltam, ahol egy hét alatt többet fejlődtem, mint egész évben. Egy táborban a napirend is izgalmasabb, mert reggeltől estig van program. A családi nyaralás mellett viszont az szól, hogy végre sok időt tölthetünk együtt, hiszen évközben mindenki sietve él. Ráadásul közösen olyan helyekre juthatunk el, ahová egy tábor nem visz el. A tábor hátránya lehet, hogy néha hiányzik az otthon, a családi út pedig drágább is lehet.
Én mégis mindkettőt szeretném: egy hetet táborban, egyet a családommal. Szerintem így lesz igazán teljes a nyár.
e2026-1: Sok külföldi filmet nézek, ezért gyakran gondolkodom azon, jobb-e felirattal vagy szinkronnal nézni őket. Mindkét megoldásnak vannak hívei.

A felirat mellett szól, hogy így halljuk a színészek eredeti hangját, ami sokat hozzátesz a játékukhoz. Ráadásul közben szinte észrevétlenül tanuljuk a nyelvet: én például sok angol kifejezést sorozatokból jegyeztem meg. A felirat ellen szól viszont, hogy az olvasás elvonja a figyelmet a képről, és egy gyors jelenetnél könnyű lemaradni. A kistestvérem még lassan olvas, ezért ő hamar elveszíti a fonalat, és unatkozni kezd. A szinkronos filmnél kényelmesen hátradőlhetünk, bár a fordítás néha nem adja vissza a poénokat. A mesefilmeket ezért a legtöbb moziban eleve szinkronnal vetítik.
Szerintem a legjobb, ha a néző választhat. Én a nyelvtanulás miatt inkább a feliratos filmeket kedvelem, de egy fárasztó nap után szívesen nézek szinkronosat is.
e2026-2: Ma már szinte mindenki játszik valamilyen online játékkal, a polcon lévő társasjátékok pedig sokszor porosodnak. Érdemes végiggondolni, melyik mit ad nekünk.

A társasjáték mellett szól, hogy egy asztal körül ülünk, közben beszélgetünk és sokat nevetünk. Nem kell hozzá képernyő, így a szemünk is pihen. Nálunk karácsonykor az egész család társasozik, és ezek a legjobb estéink. Az online játék előnye viszont, hogy azokkal a barátaimmal is játszhatok, akik messze laknak. Ezenkívül rengeteg játék közül választhatok, és nem kell senkit összeszervezni hozzá. Hátránya, hogy könnyen elszalad vele az idő, és a végén fáradtabb vagyok, mint előtte.
Úgy gondolom, mindkettőnek megvan a helye. Hétköznap jólesik egy rövid online meccs, de ha tehetem, a hétvégi közös társasozást választom.
e2025-1: Az osztályomban van, akinek három testvére van, és van, aki egyedüli gyerek. Sokszor beszélgetünk arról, kinek jobb.

A testvér mellett szól, hogy mindig van kivel játszani, és meg lehet vele beszélni azt is, amit a szüleinknek nem mondanánk el. A közös életben megtanulunk osztozni és alkalmazkodni, ami később is hasznos. Nekem van egy öcsém, és bár sokat vitatkozunk, a nyaraláson nélküle unatkoznék. Az egykék viszont több figyelmet kapnak a szüleiktől, hiszen nem kell megosztaniuk az idejüket. Saját szobájuk van, ahol nyugodtan tanulhatnak, és kevesebb otthon a veszekedés. Hátrány lehet, hogy néha magányosnak érzik magukat.
Szerintem nem az számít, hányan vagyunk, hanem az, hogy figyelünk-e egymásra. Én mégis örülök, hogy van testvérem, mert vele sosem vagyok egyedül.
e2024-1: Az osztálykirándulást minden évben nagyon várjuk. Szerintem ez nem egyszerű szórakozás, hanem a tanév egyik legfontosabb programja.

Az első érvem, hogy a kiránduláson az osztály jobban összekovácsolódik: olyanokkal is beszélgetünk, akikkel a szünetekben alig. A második, hogy új helyeket ismerünk meg, és amit a könyvből tanultunk, azt a valóságban is látjuk. Tavaly Egerben jártunk, és a vár falai között egészen más volt hallani az ostromról, mint a tanteremben. A harmadik érvem, hogy a tanárainkat is más oldalukról ismerjük meg, hiszen együtt túrázunk és játszunk velük. Ráadásul az út során megtanulunk vigyázni egymásra és a holminkra. Este a szálláson sokáig beszélgettünk, és azóta sokkal jobb a hangulat az osztályban.
Ezért úgy gondolom, hogy az osztálykirándulásra mindenképpen szükség van. Remélem, idén is lesz, mert ezekre a napokra évek múlva is emlékezni fogunk.
e2024-2: Ma már természetes, hogy a barátainkkal csetelünk vagy videón beszélgetünk. Kérdés azonban, hogy ez pótolhatja-e a személyes találkozást.

Az online beszélgetés nagy előnye, hogy azzal is tarthatjuk a kapcsolatot, aki messze lakik. A legjobb barátnőm tavaly másik városba költözött, és csak így tudunk minden nap beszélni. Személyesen viszont látjuk a másik arcát és hangulatát, ezért sokkal kevesebb a félreértés. Egy írott üzenetről sokszor nem derül ki, hogy viccnek szánták-e. A harmadik érvem, hogy a közös élmény, például egy kirándulás vagy egy jó játék, csak együtt az igazi. Amikor a barátnőm a szünetben meglátogatott, egy délután alatt többet nevettünk, mint egy hónapnyi csetelés közben.
Szerintem az online beszélgetés hasznos, de nem adhat ugyanolyan élményt, mint a találkozás. Ezért ha tehetem, inkább személyesen találkozom a barátaimmal.

a: A társasjátéknál egy asztalnál ülünk, közben beszélgetünk és nevetünk.
Nem kell hozzá képernyő, pihen a szem.
b: Online távol élő barátokkal is játszhatunk.
Rengeteg játék közül választhatunk, és bármikor elkezdhetjük.

a: Felirattal halljuk a színészek eredeti hangját.
Közben észrevétlenül tanuljuk az idegen nyelvet.
b: Az olvasás elvonja a figyelmet a képről.
A kisebbek vagy a lassabban olvasók lemaradhatnak a szövegről.

a: A táborban új barátokat szerzünk.
Megtanulunk önállóan boldogulni a szüleink nélkül.
b: A családi nyaraláson végre sok időt töltünk együtt.
Olyan helyekre is eljutunk, ahová tábor nem visz.

a: A testvérrel mindig van kivel játszani és megbeszélni a dolgokat.
Megtanulunk osztozni és alkalmazkodni.
b: Az egyke több figyelmet kap a szüleitől.
Saját szobája, nyugalma van, kevesebb a veszekedés.

a: Online is tarthatjuk a kapcsolatot azzal, aki messze lakik.
Személyesen viszont látjuk a másik arcát, hangulatát, ezért kevesebb a félreértés.
A közös élmény (sport, kirándulás, játék) csak együtt az igazi.
A kiránduláson az osztály jobban összekovácsolódik.
Új helyeket ismerünk meg, és a tanultakat a valóságban látjuk.
A tanárainkat is más oldalukról ismerjük meg.
Az ünnepség segít megérteni, mi történt a múltban.
A közös készülés (műsor, ének) összehozza az osztályt.
Megtanuljuk tisztelni azokat, akik a szabadságért küzdöttek.
Csoportban több jó ötlet születik.
Megtanulunk együttműködni és meghallgatni egymást.
b: Előfordul, hogy egy-két ember dolgozik mindenki helyett.
Nehezebb igazságosan osztályozni.

a: A nyomtatott könyvbe lehet jegyzetelni, aláhúzni.
Nem merül le, és nem tereli el a figyelmet értesítés.
b: A digitális tananyag könnyebb, nem nehéz tőle a táska.
Videó, hang, gyors keresés is van benne.

a: Több szünet mellett gyakrabban ki tudjuk pihenni magunkat.
Kevesebb a felejtés, mert nincs nagyon hosszú nyári szünet.
b: A hosszú nyári szünetben igazán ki lehet kapcsolódni, táborozni, utazni.
A nyári melegben nehéz az iskolában tanulni.

a: Csapatsportban megtanulunk összedolgozni, a siker közös.
A társak lelkesítenek, ha fáradt vagy.
b: Egyéni sportban csak rajtad múlik az eredmény.
Akkor edzhetsz, amikor neked megfelel.

a: Távoktatásban nem kell utazni, több idő marad.
A saját tempómban haladhatok.
b: Hiányoznak a barátok és a személyes magyarázat.
Otthon nehezebb figyelni, sok minden eltereli a figyelmet.

a: A moziban óriási a vászon, és jobb a hang.
A közös mozizás program, élmény a barátokkal.
b: Otthon akkor állítom meg a filmet, amikor akarom.
Olcsóbb és kényelmesebb.

a: Szóban el tudom magyarázni, amit gondolok, és a tanár rá tud kérdezni.
Fejleszti a beszédkészséget és a magabiztosságot.
b: Írásban több idő van gondolkodni.
Kevésbé izgulok, mert nem figyel közben az egész osztály.

a: A felnőtt maga dönt a saját életéről.
Saját pénze van, azt csinál, amit szeretne.
b: A gyereknek kevesebb a gondja és a felelőssége.
Több ideje jut játékra, barátokra.

a: A műsor lehetőséget ad a tehetséges fiataloknak, hogy megismerjék őket.
A nézőket is arra ösztönzi, hogy gyakoroljanak.
b: A kiesés sok néző előtt nagyon megviselő lehet.
Sokszor nem a tudás, hanem a népszerűség dönt.

a: Egyenruhában nem számít, kinek milyen drága ruhája van.
Reggel nem kell azon gondolkodni, mit vegyünk fel.
b: A ruhánkkal az egyéniségünket fejezzük ki.
Nem mindenkinek kényelmes vagy előnyös ugyanaz a ruha.

a: Előnyök (pl. iskolai tábor): együtt lehetünk a barátokkal.
Sok a szervezett program, nem unatkozunk.
b: Hátrányok: kevés a szabadidő, kötött a napirend.
Hiányozhat a család, az otthon.

a: A közösségi oldalakon könnyű tartani a kapcsolatot a barátokkal.
Gyorsan értesülünk a hírekről, programokról.
b: Rengeteg időt elvisz, és a tanulás rovására mehet.
Vigyázni kell a személyes adatokra, és előfordul bántó megjegyzés is.

p1.title: The return of the night train
paras: Twenty years ago, most people believed the sleeper train was finished. Cheap flights had made it possible to cross a continent in two hours for the price of a restaurant meal, and one overnight route after another was quietly closed. The carriages, many of them built in the 1970s, were sold off or left to rust in railway yards.

Today the picture looks rather different. New overnight services are being announced almost every year, and tickets for the most popular routes often sell out weeks in advance. What has changed is not the technology – a night train is still, basically, a hotel that moves – but the way travellers think about their journeys.

For Marta Lindqvist, who takes the sleeper to visit her sister four times a year, the attraction is simple. ‘I get on after dinner, read for an hour and fall asleep,’ she says. ‘When I wake up, I am in the city centre, not in an airport forty kilometres away.’ She admits that the ticket costs her more than a flight would. ‘But I don’t pay for a hotel, and I don’t lose a day. When I add it all up, there isn’t much difference.’

Rail companies, however, are finding the business harder than passengers might imagine. A sleeping carriage carries far fewer people than an ordinary one, and it can make only one journey per night, whereas a daytime train may run the same route four or five times. Staff must work unsocial hours, and every bed has to be cleaned and prepared again before the evening departure.

The biggest problem, though, is a shortage of carriages. Almost nobody built them during the years when night trains were unfashionable, and ordering new ones takes time: operators say they wait up to four years between signing a contract and welcoming the first passenger on board.
None of this seems to discourage travellers. Surveys suggest that people who try a night train once are very likely to do it again – and to tell their friends.

qs.q: Twenty years ago, overnight routes were closed because
opts: the carriages were too old to use.
flying had become cheap and fast.
passengers complained about the service.
qs.expl: 1. bekezdés: az olcsó repülőjegyek miatt szűntek meg a járatok („Cheap flights had made it possible…”).

qs.q: According to the writer, night trains have become popular again because
opts: travellers’ attitudes have changed.
the trains are now much faster.
the carriages are more modern.
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: nem a technika változott, hanem az, ahogyan az utazók gondolkodnak („the way travellers think”).

qs.q: Marta Lindqvist likes the night train because she
opts: can work during the journey.
pays less than she would for a flight.
arrives in the middle of the city.
qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: „When I wake up, I am in the city centre”. A jegy drágább, mint a repülő, tehát a b) nem jó.

qs.q: Marta thinks that, overall, travelling by sleeper
opts: is much more expensive than flying.
costs about the same as flying.
saves her a lot of money.
qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: „When I add it all up, there isn’t much difference.”

qs.q: One reason night trains are difficult for companies is that a sleeping carriage
opts: can only be used once each night.
needs staff who are hard to find.
cannot be cleaned quickly enough.
qs.expl: 4. bekezdés: „it can make only one journey per night”. A másik két állítás nem szerepel a szövegben.

qs.q: What is the main difficulty for operators?
opts: Passengers rarely travel a second time.
New carriages are too expensive.
There are not enough carriages.
qs.expl: 5. bekezdés: „The biggest problem … is a shortage of carriages.”

p2.title: Why we forget names
paras: You are introduced to someone at a party, you shake hands, and thirty seconds later you realise you have no idea what they are called. (1) ______ In fact, it happens to almost everybody, and it has very little to do with intelligence.

One explanation is that names are, in a sense, meaningless. If you learn that a woman is a baker, your brain immediately connects the word with bread, early mornings and the smell of a warm shop. (2) ______ There is nothing for the memory to hold on to.

A second reason is that we are often not really listening. At the moment of introduction, most of us are thinking about ourselves: how we look, what we are going to say next, whether our handshake is too weak. (3) ______

Fortunately, there are a few simple techniques that help. The first is to repeat the name aloud as soon as you hear it – ‘Nice to meet you, Daniel.’ (4) ______ Another is to link the name to something you can picture. If Daniel has thick, curly hair, you might imagine a lion wearing his glasses. (5) ______
Finally, do not be afraid to ask again. (6) ______ They are far more likely to be pleased that you care enough to get it right.
sents: The sillier the image, the better it tends to stick.
Most people will not be offended.
Many people assume this is a sign of a poor memory.
As a result, the name passes by while our attention is somewhere else.
If you learn that her name is Baker, however, no such picture appears.
Saying it forces you to pay attention to it.
Some names are simply more common than others.
expl: Az „In fact, it happens to almost everybody” erre a feltevésre válaszol.
A „however” a pék foglalkozás és a Baker név közti ellentétet jelzi.
Az „As a result” a figyelmetlenség következményét adja meg.
Az „it” a hangosan kimondott névre utal.
Az „image” az előző mondat elképzelt képére utal.
A „They” a következő mondatban a „Most people”-re utal.

texts: Wheelhouse Cycles – end-of-season sale. All city and touring bikes are reduced by up to 30% until the end of October. Every bicycle is checked by our mechanics before it leaves the shop, and your first service is free. Not sure which size you need? Book a twenty-minute fitting session and try before you buy. Open Tuesday to Saturday, 9 till 6.

We set off from the coast at seven, hoping to reach the mountain hut before dark. By midday the wind was so strong that I had to get off and push, and then the rain started. My brother, who had insisted we didn’t need waterproof jackets, stopped talking altogether. We arrived soaked and exhausted – and I would do it again tomorrow.

Riverside Cycling Club meets every Sunday at 9 a.m. outside the old town hall. Rides are between 30 and 60 kilometres and nobody is left behind: an experienced member always cycles at the back. New riders are welcome to come along twice before deciding whether to become members. The annual fee includes insurance and a club shirt.

Each year, most collisions involving cyclists happen at junctions, often because a driver simply has not seen the rider. Wear something bright during the day and use lights at both ends of the bike after sunset – a rear light alone is not enough. Check your brakes once a week, and never assume that the driver of a turning lorry knows you are beside it.

qs.q: Which text describes a personal experience?
qs.expl: A B szöveg egyes szám első személyű élménybeszámoló.

qs.q: Which text is trying to sell something?
qs.expl: Az A szöveg egy kerékpárbolt akciós hirdetése.

qs.q: Which text gives advice on avoiding danger?
qs.expl: A D szöveg közlekedésbiztonsági tanácsokat ad.

qs.q: How can you find out if a bike is the right size for you?
qs.expl: A: „Book a twenty-minute fitting session”.

qs.q: What was the weather like on a journey?
qs.expl: B: erős szél, majd eső.

qs.q: How many times can you take part before joining?
qs.expl: C: „come along twice before deciding”.

qs.q: How often should you examine part of your bicycle?
qs.expl: D: „Check your brakes once a week”.

p4.title: The lighthouse at Saltmarsh Point
paras: For more than a century, the lighthouse at Saltmarsh Point guided fishing boats safely past the rocks at the mouth of the bay. It was built in 1884, after a storm in which three boats were lost in a single night, and the money was raised not by the government but by the fishermen’s families themselves.

The first keeper, Thomas Reed, lived in the tower with his wife and five children. His main duty was to keep the oil lamp burning from sunset to sunrise, which meant climbing the 112 steps several times every night. In thick fog, when the light could not be seen, he rang a large bell by hand, sometimes for hours.

Electricity reached the lighthouse in 1931, and the work became easier. The last keeper left in 1978, when the light was made fully automatic, and for the next twenty years the building stood empty. Windows were broken, and seabirds nested on the staircase.

In 1999 a group of local volunteers decided to save it. They spent four summers repairing the roof and repainting the tower in its original red and white stripes. Today the ground floor is a small museum, and the keeper’s rooms can be rented by visitors who want to spend a night above the sea. The income from these guests pays for the building’s repairs.

The light itself still works, although ships now rely on satellite navigation. It is switched on once a year, on the anniversary of the 1884 storm, when the people of the village gather on the beach to watch.

qs.q: What event led to the building of the lighthouse?
qs.show: a storm / three boats were lost
qs.expl: 1. bekezdés: egy vihar után épült, amelyben három hajó odaveszett.

qs.q: Who paid for the lighthouse?
qs.expl: 1. bekezdés: a pénzt a halászok családjai gyűjtötték össze.

qs.q: What did the keeper use to warn boats in fog?
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: ködben kézzel harangozott.

qs.q: In which year did the last keeper leave?
qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: „The last keeper left in 1978”.

qs.q: How long did the volunteers’ repairs take?
qs.expl: 4. bekezdés: „They spent four summers repairing…”.

qs.q: What pays for the building’s repairs today?
qs.show: income from guests / renting the rooms
qs.expl: 4. bekezdés: a vendégektől származó bevétel.

qs.q: How often is the light switched on now?
qs.expl: 5. bekezdés: évente egyszer, a vihar évfordulóján.

p1.title: A school without bells
paras: When Hollin Park School switched off its bells three years ago, some teachers predicted chaos. For decades a loud electric ring had told twelve hundred students when to sit down, when to stand up and when to eat. Without it, the critics said, nobody would arrive anywhere on time.

The idea came from the head teacher, Irene Castell, after a visit to a hospital where her mother was being treated. ‘Hundreds of people worked there, and all of them were where they needed to be, without any bells at all,’ she says. ‘I started to wonder what exactly we were teaching our students by ringing one every fifty minutes.’

The first weeks were, she admits, difficult. Students drifted into lessons several minutes late, and a few teachers kept talking long after their classes should have finished. But instead of bringing the bells back, the school put a clock in every corridor and asked teachers to end each lesson with a two-minute summary, so that everyone knew the lesson was closing.

By the end of the first term, lateness had fallen below the level recorded in the year before the change. More surprisingly, teachers reported that the corridors had become calmer. ‘The bell used to send everybody out at exactly the same second, like the start of a race,’ says Castell. ‘Now classes leave over two or three minutes, and nobody is pushed.’

Not everyone is convinced. Some parents feel that young people need firm signals, and one teacher, who asked not to be named, said he still missed ‘the certainty’ of the bell. Students themselves seem to have fewer doubts. In a survey last spring, more than eight out of ten said they would not want the bells back, and many added that they now wore a watch for the first time in their lives.
Several other schools in the region have since asked Hollin Park for advice. Castell’s answer is always the same: ‘Try it for one term. You can always switch the bells on again.’

qs.q: Before the change, some teachers believed that
opts: students would be late for lessons.
lessons would become shorter.
students would eat at the wrong times.
qs.expl: 1. bekezdés: „nobody would arrive anywhere on time”.

qs.q: Irene Castell got the idea
opts: from another school she had visited.
as a result of visiting a hospital.
from a member of her family.
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: egy kórházi látogatás során figyelt fel rá; az édesanyja csak beteg volt ott, az ötlet nem tőle származik.

qs.q: When problems appeared at the beginning, the school
opts: returned to the old system for a while.
punished the students who were late.
introduced some practical changes.
qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: órákat tettek a folyosókra, és a tanárok összefoglalóval zárják az órát.

qs.q: After one term,
opts: fewer students were late than before the change.
lateness was the same as before.
teachers were finishing lessons early.
qs.expl: 4. bekezdés: „lateness had fallen below the level recorded in the year before the change”.

qs.q: Castell says the corridors are calmer because
opts: there are fewer students in them.
students do not all leave at once.
teachers now watch the corridors.
qs.expl: 4. bekezdés: az osztályok két-három perc alatt, nem egyszerre mennek ki.

qs.q: What do most students think?
opts: They miss the certainty of the bell.
They are unsure about the change.
They prefer the school without bells.
qs.expl: 5. bekezdés: tízből több mint nyolcan nem kérnék vissza a csengőt. A „certainty” egy tanár véleménye.

p2.title: Learning to juggle
paras: Last January I decided to learn something completely useless. I had spent the whole of the previous year studying for exams, and I wanted a skill that nobody would ever test. (1) ______ All I needed, according to a video I found online, was three tennis balls and a little patience.
The video made it look easy. (2) ______ I spent most of the first evening on my knees, looking for balls under the sofa, while my younger brother laughed at me from the doorway.

After a week of failure I changed my approach and went back to the beginning. Instead of three balls, I practised with one, throwing it from hand to hand in a gentle curve. (3) ______ But after two days my hands had started to move without my thinking about it, and I added a second ball.
The real breakthrough came about a month later. (4) ______ I counted ten catches, then twenty, and then I dropped everything because I was so surprised.

What I did not expect was how the practice would affect the rest of my life. I am usually an impatient person who gives up when things go wrong. (5) ______ I find I now approach maths problems in the same way, breaking them into smaller steps.
I still cannot juggle four balls, and I have no plans to join a circus. (6) ______ My brother, by the way, has asked me to teach him.
sents: It felt ridiculous, like learning to walk again.
Juggling seemed perfect.
One evening, without warning, the three balls simply stayed in the air.
In reality, it was anything but.
But I can do something that I could not do a year ago, and that is enough.
Dropping a ball two hundred times a day has changed that.
The balls were more expensive than I had expected.
expl: Az előző mondat ilyen készséget keres, a zsonglőrködés erre „tökéletes”.
Az „anything but” az „easy”-re felel: a valóságban egyáltalán nem volt könnyű.
Az „It felt ridiculous” az egy labdával való gyakorlásra utal; utána „But” jön.
A „breakthrough” maga az a pillanat, amikor a három labda a levegőben maradt.
A „that” a türelmetlenségre utal, amely megváltozott.
A „But” ellentétet állít a „cannot juggle four balls” mondattal.

texts: Greenway Animal Shelter needs you! We are looking for volunteers aged sixteen or over to walk dogs at weekends. No experience is necessary, as full training is given on your first morning. All we ask is that you can come at least twice a month. Call in any Saturday before noon to fill in a form.

I only signed up at the food bank because my friend didn’t want to go alone. On my first evening I packed four hundred bags of rice and my arms ached for two days. But then an elderly man thanked me as if I had given him a present, and I understood why people keep coming back. That was three years ago.

Students from Castle Road College collected more than two tonnes of rubbish from the river bank last Saturday. The clean-up, organised by the college’s environment club, attracted ninety volunteers, almost twice as many as last year. The mayor, who joined them for the morning, promised that the council would provide gloves and bags for future events.

Thinking of volunteering abroad? Choose carefully. Ask the organisation exactly where your fee goes, and be suspicious of any project that accepts everyone without an interview. A good programme will expect you to stay for at least a month, because shorter visits rarely help the local community. Speak to former volunteers before you pay anything.

qs.q: Which text is looking for new people?
qs.expl: Az A szöveg önkénteseket toboroz.

qs.q: Which text warns readers to be careful?
qs.expl: A D szöveg óvatosságra int („Choose carefully”).

qs.q: Which text reports on a recent event?
qs.expl: A C szöveg hír a múlt szombati szemétszedésről.

qs.q: Why did somebody start volunteering?
qs.expl: B: mert a barátja nem akart egyedül menni.

qs.q: How often must volunteers be available?
qs.expl: A: „at least twice a month”.

qs.q: Who has agreed to supply equipment?
qs.expl: C: az önkormányzat ad kesztyűt és zsákot.

qs.q: What should you do before handing over money?
qs.expl: D: „Speak to former volunteers before you pay anything.”

p4.title: The village bookshop
paras: When the only bookshop in the village of Aldermere closed in 2015, most residents assumed it had gone for good. The owner had retired, and nobody wanted to buy a business that had been losing money for years. The building, a former bakery on the main square, remained empty for eighteen months.

It was a retired teacher, Joan Whitlock, who suggested that the village should run the shop itself. At a public meeting she proposed selling shares at twenty pounds each, so that almost anyone could afford to become an owner. Within three months, more than four hundred people had bought one, and the shop reopened the following spring.

The new bookshop is not quite like the old one. Because it has only one paid employee, the manager, most of the work is done by a team of around thirty volunteers. One corner has become a café, which now brings in nearly half of the shop’s income. On Thursday evenings the tables are pushed back for talks by visiting authors, and tickets usually sell out.

The shop’s most unusual service is aimed at people who cannot easily leave their homes. Twice a week, volunteers deliver books by bicycle to elderly residents in Aldermere and two neighbouring villages, and stay for a conversation if they are invited.

Last year the bookshop made a small profit for the first time. The shareholders voted to spend it not on themselves but on books for the primary school library. ‘Nobody bought a share to get rich,’ says Whitlock. ‘We bought them because a village without a bookshop felt like a house without windows.’

qs.q: What was the bookshop building originally?
qs.expl: 1. bekezdés: „a former bakery”.

qs.q: How long was the building empty?
qs.expl: 1. bekezdés: „remained empty for eighteen months”.

qs.q: How much did one share cost?
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: „shares at twenty pounds each”.

qs.q: Who does most of the work in the shop?
qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: mintegy harminc önkéntes.

qs.q: What provides almost half of the shop’s income?
qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: a kávézó hozza a bevétel közel felét.

qs.q: How are books delivered to elderly residents?
qs.expl: 4. bekezdés: „deliver books by bicycle”.

qs.q: What was last year’s profit spent on?
qs.expl: 5. bekezdés: az általános iskola könyvtárának vettek könyveket.

p1.title: Three weeks on a research ship
paras: Most seventeen-year-olds spend the summer holidays as far from a classroom as possible. Eli Navarro spent his in a floating laboratory. Last July he was one of six students chosen from more than nine hundred applicants to join the research ship Meridian for three weeks, as it measured water temperature along a line across the North Atlantic.

Eli had applied without much hope. ‘My science marks are good, but not the best in my class,’ he says. ‘I think they chose me because of my letter. I wrote about repairing engines with my grandfather, and it turned out the ship needed people who were useful with their hands.’

Life on board was nothing like he had imagined. The students worked in four-hour shifts, like the rest of the crew, which meant that he was sometimes woken at three in the morning to lower instruments into the sea. For the first few days he was too seasick to eat anything except dry bread. ‘Nobody laughed,’ he remembers. ‘The captain told me she had felt exactly the same on her first voyage.’

The work itself was often repetitive. The same measurements had to be taken at the same depths, again and again, and every figure was written down twice, by two different people. At first Eli found this boring. Then one of the scientists showed him how a single careless number could ruin a result that had taken ten years to collect. ‘After that I checked everything three times,’ he says.

What he valued most, however, was not the science but the conversations. With no internet connection for most of the voyage, the crew spent their free hours talking, playing cards and telling stories. ‘I learned more about people in three weeks than in three years at school,’ Eli says.
He still intends to study engineering rather than oceanography. But he has already applied to return to the Meridian next summer – this time as a paid assistant.

qs.q: Eli took part in a voyage which
opts: was organised by his school.
accepted only a few students.
lasted the whole summer.
qs.expl: 1. bekezdés: több mint kilencszáz jelentkezőből hatan kerültek be; az út három hétig tartott.

qs.q: Eli believes he was selected because of
opts: his practical skills.
his excellent marks in science.
his grandfather’s connections.
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: a hajón ügyes kezű emberekre volt szükség; a jegyei nem a legjobbak.

qs.q: During the first days on the ship, Eli
opts: was laughed at by the crew.
could not sleep at night.
felt ill.
qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: tengeribeteg volt („too seasick to eat”); senki sem nevette ki.

qs.q: Eli began to take the measurements seriously when
opts: he made a serious mistake.
a scientist explained the effect of errors.
the captain checked his work.
qs.expl: 4. bekezdés: egy kutató megmutatta, hogy egyetlen hibás szám tíz év munkáját teheti tönkre.

qs.q: What did Eli appreciate most about the voyage?
opts: the scientific knowledge he gained
the time he spent with other people
being without the internet
qs.expl: 5. bekezdés: „not the science but the conversations”.

qs.q: In the future, Eli plans to
opts: become an oceanographer.
work on the ship without pay.
go back to the same ship.
qs.expl: 6. bekezdés: jelentkezett, hogy jövő nyáron visszatérjen, fizetett asszisztensként; mérnöknek készül.

p2.title: Board-game cafés
paras: Ten years ago, if you wanted to play a board game, you invited friends to your home and hoped that nobody lost any of the pieces. Today, in many cities, you can simply walk into a café. (1) ______ For a small fee, usually charged per hour, customers may choose any of them and play for as long as they like.

The idea is surprisingly simple, but it solves a real problem. Modern board games are expensive, and it is impossible to know whether you will enjoy one before you buy it. (2) ______ If the game turns out to be dull, you put it back and take another.
Most cafés also employ staff whose only job is to explain the rules. (3) ______ With a ‘game guide’ at the table, a group can be playing within five minutes.

Owners say their customers are more varied than people expect. (4) ______ There are grandparents with grandchildren, colleagues after work and couples on a first date, who find that a game gives them something to talk about.

The cafés do face one difficulty. A table of four people who play a single game for three hours may order only a couple of drinks each. (5) ______ This is why most places charge for time rather than relying on what people eat and drink.
Whether the fashion will last is hard to say. (6) ______ For the moment, though, on a rainy Saturday afternoon it can be difficult to find a free table.
sents: Selling coffee alone would never cover the rent.
Its shelves hold hundreds of games, from old favourites to the latest releases.
Some games can be finished in less than ten minutes.
This matters, because reading a thirty-page instruction booklet is nobody’s idea of fun.
Similar trends have disappeared as quickly as they arrived.
A café lets you try it first.
They are certainly not all students or teenagers.
expl: Az „Its shelves” a kávézóra utal, a következő mondat „any of them”-je pedig a játékokra.
Az „it” a megvenni kívánt játékra utal: előbb kipróbálhatod.
A „This matters” a szabályokat elmagyarázó személyzetre vonatkozik.
A „They” a vendégekre utal, utána jön a felsorolás.
A kevés fogyasztás következménye: a kávéból nem jönne ki a bérleti díj.
Bizonytalanság a jövőről; a „For the moment, though” ezzel áll ellentétben.

texts: The Harbour Museum is open daily from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., except on Mondays. Entry is free for under-18s and for everyone on the first Sunday of each month. Large bags must be left in the lockers by the entrance, which take a one-euro coin. Guided tours in English begin at 11 and 2 and do not need to be booked.

I had expected an hour of dusty glass cases. Instead, the new Museum of Sound kept my two children busy for an entire afternoon. They recorded their own voices, built a drum from a paint tin and refused to leave the ‘silent room’. My only complaint is the café, where a sandwich costs more than our tickets did.

The City Science Museum is looking for weekend guides to work in its new space gallery. You should enjoy talking to children and be able to explain complicated ideas simply. A science degree is not required, but you must speak at least two languages. Applications close on 30 April; interviews will be held in May.

I was sorry to read that the council plans to move the Railway Museum out of the old station. The building is the most important exhibit of all: generations of local people began their working lives there. A modern hall on the edge of town may be cheaper to heat, but it will have no history. I urge readers to sign the petition.

qs.expl: D: helyiek nemzedékei kezdték ott a munkát, története van.

p4.title: The market that came back
paras: Marlow Bridge had held a market every Friday since the Middle Ages, but by 2008 it had almost disappeared. A large supermarket had opened on the edge of the town, with free parking and long opening hours, and one by one the market traders gave up. In the final year only three stalls remained, selling cheap socks, phone covers and second-hand DVDs.

The market was rescued by a cheese-maker named Peter Oakes. He had noticed that visitors to his farm were prepared to drive long distances for food they could not find in shops, and he persuaded the council to let him organise a single trial market. He invited only people who produced what they sold. Twenty-two farmers, bakers and beekeepers came, and by eleven o’clock most of them had nothing left.

The council agreed to make the market permanent, but Oakes insisted on two rules. Nothing on sale could come from further than fifty kilometres away, and every stall had to offer free samples, so that customers could taste before buying.

The effect on the town was greater than anyone had predicted. Shops around the square, several of which had been empty, were rented again, because people who came for the market stayed to look around. A survey found that market-day visitors spent an average of two hours in the town centre.

Even the supermarket has changed its mind. After years of ignoring the market, it now runs a free bus between its car park and the square every Friday morning. ‘They finally understood,’ says Oakes, ‘that we bring people to the town, and some of those people need washing powder as well as cheese.’

qs.q: How often was the market traditionally held?
qs.expl: 1. bekezdés: „a market every Friday”.

qs.q: What caused the market to decline?
qs.expl: 1. bekezdés: a város szélén megnyílt szupermarket.

qs.q: What was Peter Oakes’s job?
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: „a cheese-maker named Peter Oakes”.

qs.q: How many traders came to the trial market?
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: „Twenty-two farmers, bakers and beekeepers”.

qs.q: What did every stall have to offer?
qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: ingyenes kóstoló.

qs.q: How long did visitors stay in the town centre?
qs.expl: 4. bekezdés: átlagosan két órát.

qs.q: What does the supermarket provide on Fridays?
qs.expl: 5. bekezdés: ingyenes buszjárat a parkoló és a tér között.

p1.title: A year without new clothes
paras: When Nora Feld announced that she would not buy any new clothes for a year, her friends assumed it was a joke. At sixteen, she had been the one who always knew which shop had a sale, and her wardrobe was so full that the door no longer closed properly.

The idea came from a school project. Her geography class had been asked to find out where one object they owned had been made, and Nora chose a T-shirt that had cost her less than a sandwich. She traced it to three different countries and worked out that it had travelled further than she had in her whole life. ‘I had worn it twice,’ she says. ‘That was what shocked me, not the price.’

The rules she set herself were strict but not impossible. Second-hand clothes were allowed, and so were presents, but she could not ask for them. Anything that tore had to be mended rather than replaced. Her mother, who had expected the experiment to end within a month, taught her to sew on a machine that had stood unused in the attic for years.

The first weeks were the hardest. Nora found that she had been visiting shopping websites several times a day without really noticing, ‘the way other people check the weather’. She deleted the apps from her phone, and filled the time by sorting out what she already owned. To her surprise, she discovered eleven items that still had their labels on.

By the spring her classmates had stopped teasing and started asking questions. Two of them joined her, and together they organised a clothes-swap evening in the school hall, to which more than a hundred students brought things they no longer wore. The event has since been repeated every term.

The year ended last month. Nora has not hurried back to the shops. ‘I’m not against buying things,’ she says. ‘I bought a winter coat last week, and I love it. But I thought about it for a fortnight first – and that’s the habit I want to keep.’

qs.q: Before the experiment, Nora’s friends thought of her as someone who
opts: had little interest in fashion.
was keen on shopping.
often played jokes on people.
qs.expl: 1. bekezdés: mindig tudta, hol van leárazás, és tele volt a szekrénye.

qs.q: What surprised Nora most about her T-shirt?
opts: how rarely she had used it
how cheap it had been
how many countries had produced it
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: „I had worn it twice … That was what shocked me, not the price.”

qs.q: According to her rules, Nora could
opts: request clothes as gifts.
replace clothes that were damaged.
get clothes that somebody had worn before.
qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: használt ruha megengedett; ajándékot kérni nem lehetett, a szakadtat meg kellett javítani.

qs.q: Nora’s mother
opts: doubted that Nora would continue for long.
refused to support the idea.
bought her a sewing machine.
qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: az anyja arra számított, hogy egy hónapon belül vége lesz; a gép a padláson állt.

qs.q: In the first weeks, Nora realised that she
opts: had more free time than she needed.
had looked at online shops out of habit.
owned fewer clothes than she had thought.
qs.expl: 4. bekezdés: naponta többször nézte a webáruházakat, „without really noticing”.

qs.q: Now that the year is over, Nora
opts: has decided never to buy new clothes.
regrets buying a coat.
intends to choose more carefully.
qs.expl: 6. bekezdés: két hétig gondolkodott a kabáton, és ezt a szokást szeretné megtartani.

p2.title: Tiny forests
paras: On a piece of land no bigger than a tennis court, between a car park and a block of flats, six hundred young trees are growing so close together that it is hard to walk between them. (1) ______ It is one of thousands of ‘tiny forests’ that have been planted in towns around the world over the past decade.

The method is different from ordinary tree planting. Instead of putting a few trees of the same kind in neat rows, volunteers plant thirty or forty local species very densely. (2) ______ As a result, a tiny forest can grow up to ten times faster than a conventional one.
For the first two or three years the forest needs regular attention. (3) ______ After that it is left completely alone, and no further work is necessary.
Supporters say the benefits appear remarkably quickly. (4) ______ The trees also keep the surrounding streets cooler in summer and absorb rainwater that would otherwise flood the drains.

Not everyone is convinced. Some experts point out that such a small area can store only a little carbon, and that the cost per tree is high. (5) ______ Even the critics admit, however, that the projects have one clear advantage: they are usually planted by local schoolchildren.
A child who has planted a tree tends to come back to see how it is doing. (6) ______ That, perhaps, matters more than any figure.
sents: It must be watered in dry weather, and weeds have to be pulled out by hand.
This is not a garden that somebody has forgotten to look after.
The same money, they argue, would protect a much larger area of existing woodland.
Most of the trees were imported from abroad.
The young plants have to compete for light, so they shoot upwards.
Years later, many still think of the forest as their own.
Birds and insects that have not been seen in the area for years often return within months.
expl: A sűrűn nőtt fák elhanyagolt kertnek tűnhetnek; a következő „It is one of…” ezt pontosítja.
A sűrű ültetés következménye: a növények a fényért versenyeznek, ezért gyorsan nőnek („As a result…”).
A „regular attention” kifejtése: öntözés és gyomlálás; utána „After that it is left alone”.
Az első gyorsan megjelenő előny; a következő mondat „also” szava újabb előnyt tesz hozzá.
A „they argue” a kritikus szakértőkre utal, és a magas költséghez kapcsolódik.
A „many” a fát ültető gyerekekre utal, akik visszajárnak.

texts: Cyclists using the riverside path are reminded that it is shared with pedestrians. Please keep to the left, ring your bell before overtaking and do not exceed 15 km/h. Between 1 November and 28 February the section under the railway bridge is closed after dark because of the risk of ice.

City Wheels has more than two hundred bicycles for hire at eight stations across the centre. The first thirty minutes are free; after that you pay one euro per half hour. A helmet and a lock are included, and children’s seats are available at the Central Square station only. You will need a bank card to register.

I gave up the bus six months ago, mostly to save money. What I did not expect was how much better I would feel. I arrive at work awake, I no longer worry about timetables, and I have lost four kilos without trying. Rain is still miserable, though, and I have had two punctures in one week.

The new cycle lane on Mill Road looks impressive, but whoever designed it has clearly never ridden a bike. It ends suddenly at the busiest junction in town, exactly where riders need protection most. Until the council connects it to the lane on Park Street, parents like me will go on driving our children to school.

p4.title: The clock of Brenmoor
paras: For as long as anyone in Brenmoor could remember, the clock on the town hall tower had shown the wrong time. It had stopped at twenty past four one afternoon in 1961, when a storm damaged the mechanism, and the council of the day decided that repairing it would be too expensive. Over the years people grew fond of it. Local children were told that it was always time for tea in Brenmoor.

In 2015 a retired watchmaker called Helen Draycott moved to the town. She asked to see the clock out of professional curiosity, and found that the damage was much less serious than everyone believed. Most of the parts were in good condition; only two wheels were broken, and the whole mechanism was covered in pigeon feathers. She offered to repair it without payment, on condition that the council paid for the materials.

The work took her fourteen months. Because the original drawings had been lost, she had to measure every part and make the missing wheels herself in her garage. Pupils from the secondary school helped to clean the mechanism, and one of them, a fifteen-year-old named Tom Reeve, came so often that she began to teach him the trade.

Not everybody welcomed the project. A group of residents collected almost four hundred signatures asking for the clock to be left as it was, arguing that the stopped hands were part of the town’s character. The council found a compromise. The clock would run again, but a small painted clock face showing twenty past four would be placed beside the entrance of the town hall.
The clock was restarted on New Year’s Eve. Helen Draycott has since moved away to live near her daughter, and the person who now climbs the ninety-one steps every week to wind it is Tom Reeve.

qs.q: What damaged the clock in 1961?
qs.expl: 1. bekezdés: „a storm damaged the mechanism”.

qs.q: What was Helen Draycott’s job before she retired?
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: „a retired watchmaker”.

qs.q: What did the council have to pay for?
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: ingyen dolgozott, ha a tanács kifizeti az anyagokat.

qs.q: How long did the repair take?
qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: „The work took her fourteen months.”

qs.q: Where did Helen make the missing wheels?
qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: a garázsában készítette el őket.

qs.q: How many signatures did the opponents collect?
qs.expl: 4. bekezdés: majdnem négyszáz aláírás.

qs.q: Who winds the clock now?
qs.expl: 5. bekezdés: hetente Tom Reeve megy fel felhúzni.

p1.title: The teenage referee
paras: Every Saturday morning, while most of his classmates are still asleep, fifteen-year-old Dario Kessler puts on a black shirt and walks to the local football ground. He is not there to play. For the past year he has been a referee in the under-twelve league, which makes him the youngest official in his region.

He took the course because of an injury. A broken ankle kept him out of his own team for four months, and his coach suggested refereeing as a way of staying close to the game. Dario agreed mainly because he was bored. ‘I thought I knew the rules,’ he says. ‘The first lesson showed me that I knew about half of them.’

Running a match turned out to be far more tiring than playing in one. A player can rest when the ball is at the other end of the pitch; a referee has to follow it everywhere, and must make a decision every few seconds. After his first game Dario slept for eleven hours.

The children, he says, are never the problem. They may argue for a moment, but they accept a decision and get on with the match. Their parents are a different matter. On one occasion a father shouted at him for so long that the game had to be stopped. Dario walked over, explained calmly why he had given the free kick, and offered the man his whistle. The father sat down, and the other parents applauded.

His own playing has changed as a result. He used to complain loudly whenever a decision went against him; now he says nothing, because he knows how the pitch looks from the middle. His coach has noticed something else: Dario reads the game better, and is rarely caught out of position.

The league pays him a small fee for each match, which he is saving. He has no plans to give up playing, but he has already signed up for the next level of the referees’ course, which would allow him to take charge of adult games when he turns eighteen.

qs.q: Dario is unusual because he
opts: plays in an under-twelve league.
referees at a very young age.
trains early on Saturday mornings.
qs.expl: 1. bekezdés: ő a régió legfiatalabb játékvezetője.

qs.q: Why did Dario agree to take the referees’ course?
opts: He had little else to do while he was injured.
He wanted to learn the rules properly.
His team was short of referees.
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: „Dario agreed mainly because he was bored.”

qs.q: What did Dario discover in his first lesson?
opts: that the course would be easy
that the rules had recently changed
that his knowledge was incomplete
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: a szabályoknak csak körülbelül a felét ismerte.

qs.q: Compared with playing, refereeing
opts: demands more constant effort.
allows more time to rest.
requires less concentration.
qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: a játékvezető mindenhová követi a labdát, és folyamatosan döntenie kell.

qs.q: When a father shouted at him, Dario
opts: ended the match.
asked the other parents for help.
reacted politely.
qs.expl: 4. bekezdés: nyugodtan elmagyarázta a döntését („explained calmly”).

qs.q: As a player, Dario now
opts: argues with referees more often.
accepts decisions quietly.
plays in a different position.
qs.expl: 5. bekezdés: régen hangosan panaszkodott, most nem szól semmit.

p2.title: The science of queues
paras: Nobody enjoys queuing, yet most of us spend several days of our lives each year doing exactly that. (1) ______ Their findings explain why two queues of the same length can feel completely different.

The first discovery is that occupied time feels shorter than empty time. (2) ______ People who could look at themselves while they waited stopped complaining, although the lifts were no faster than before.
Uncertainty makes things worse. A delay of ten minutes is easier to bear if you are told about it in advance. (3) ______ Passengers rarely look at them for long, but simply knowing is enough.
Fairness matters even more than speed. (4) ______ We would rather wait longer in an orderly line than a shorter time in a confused crowd.

This explains a change that many banks and airports have made. Instead of several separate lines, customers now stand in one long queue that feeds all the desks. (5) ______ Nobody, however, has to watch the line next to them moving faster.
Finally, the end of a wait colours our memory of the whole. (6) ______ Shops that understand this put their friendliest staff at the tills.
sents: Psychologists have been studying the experience for decades.
The total waiting time is almost exactly the same.
Screens showing the number of minutes until the next bus work on the same principle.
Queuing is far less common than it used to be.
If the last few minutes pass quickly and pleasantly, we forget how slow the beginning was.
This is why mirrors were once put up beside the lifts in tall office buildings.
Few things annoy us as much as watching somebody who arrived later being served first.
expl: A „Their findings” a pszichológusokra utal vissza.
A tükör elfoglaltságot ad; a következő mondat arról szól, hogy az emberek nézték magukat a liftnél.
A „them” a kijelzőkre utal; a „same principle” az előre közölt késés elve.
A méltányosság példája: bosszantó, ha a később érkezőt szolgálják ki előbb.
Az egyetlen hosszú sor nem gyorsabb, „however” senkinek sem kell a szomszéd sort néznie.
A várakozás vége határozza meg az emléket; ezért ülnek a legkedvesebb dolgozók a pénztárnál.

texts: Lingua Hub offers evening courses in nine languages, from complete beginner to advanced. Groups never have more than eight students, and all our teachers are native speakers. Term begins on 12 September. Book before the end of August and receive a ten per cent discount. A free trial lesson is available on request.

I have been using WordTrail for three months now. The short daily exercises are well designed, and the reminders are hard to ignore. However, it teaches you to recognise words rather than to use them. After ninety days I can read a menu in Portuguese, but I still cannot order from one. Good as an extra, not as a course.

If you want to remember new vocabulary, stop writing long lists. Research suggests that we learn words best when we meet them several times in different situations. Read something you enjoy, note down only five expressions a day, and try to use each of them in conversation before the week is over.

You asked how my exchange year is going. Honestly, the first month was awful: I understood nothing at dinner and went to bed with a headache every night. Then, some time in November, I realised I had laughed at a joke without translating it first. My host family say I now argue like a local.

p4.title: The cook at the end of the world
paras: When people imagine life on an Antarctic research station, they think of scientists. Yet the person the scientists themselves value most is usually the cook. At Halvorsen Base, where twenty-four people spend the dark winter months cut off from the rest of the world, that person is Ingrid Solberg, who gave up a job in a hotel kitchen in Bergen to work there.

Her greatest challenge is planning. A supply ship reaches the base only once a year, in January, so she has to order twelve months of food at once. Nothing can be forgotten: one year a previous cook ran out of coffee in August, and the story is still told as a warning.

Fresh food is the first thing to disappear. Apples and potatoes last for a few months if they are stored carefully, but salad is gone within two weeks. To solve the problem, Ingrid grows lettuce and herbs under lamps in a small heated room that the crew call the garden. It produces only about a kilo of leaves a week, but people queue to look at something green.

She has learned that food is about much more than hunger. During the winter, when the sun does not rise for almost four months, meals are the only events that divide the day. Ingrid therefore bakes bread every morning, because she believes its smell makes the station feel like a home. On Saturdays she serves dinner by candlelight, and everyone is expected to change out of their work clothes.

Birthdays receive special attention. Each person may choose the menu, and Ingrid keeps a notebook in which she writes down everybody’s favourite dish as soon as they arrive. She plans to stay for one more winter before returning to Norway, where she hopes to open a small restaurant of her own.

qs.q: Where did Ingrid work before she came to the base?
qs.expl: 1. bekezdés: egy bergeni szálloda konyháján dolgozott.

qs.q: In which month does the supply ship arrive?
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: évente egyszer, januárban.

qs.q: What did a previous cook run out of?
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: augusztusban elfogyott a kávé.

qs.q: What do the crew call the heated room?
qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: „a small heated room that the crew call the garden”.

qs.q: What does Ingrid bake every morning?
qs.expl: 4. bekezdés: minden reggel kenyeret süt.

qs.q: How is dinner served on Saturdays?
qs.expl: 4. bekezdés: szombaton gyertyafénynél vacsoráznak.

qs.q: Where does Ingrid write down people’s favourite dishes?
qs.expl: 5. bekezdés: egy füzetbe írja fel.

p1.title: The youngest beekeeper in town
paras: Amira Holt was eleven when a swarm of bees settled in the apple tree behind her family’s house. Her father wanted to call somebody to remove them. Amira, who had been watching them through the kitchen window for two days, asked whether they could stay.

A neighbour who kept bees agreed to help, on one condition: Amira would have to do the work herself. He lent her an old hive and a suit that was far too big, and for the first summer he stood behind her every time she opened the lid. ‘He never touched anything,’ she says. ‘He just told me to slow down. Bees notice when you are in a hurry.’

Five years later she has nine hives on a piece of land at the edge of town that belongs to the local primary school. In exchange for using it, she gives talks to the pupils and lets them watch through a glass panel that she fitted to one of the hives.

The honey sells out quickly at the Saturday market, but Amira insists that it has never been the point. What fascinates her is how the colony makes decisions. ‘There is a queen, but she doesn’t give orders,’ she explains. ‘Thousands of bees somehow agree on where to go and what to do, and nobody is in charge. I still don’t fully understand it, and that’s why I can’t stop.’

It has not all been easy. Two winters ago she lost four colonies to disease, and seriously thought about giving up. What changed her mind was a message from a seven-year-old who had heard her talk at school and wanted to know when the bees would be coming back.
She is now preparing to study biology at university. The hives will remain where they are: three of her former listeners, now teenagers themselves, have promised to look after them.

qs.q: When the bees first arrived, Amira
opts: was afraid of them.
wanted to keep them.
tried to move them herself.
qs.expl: 1. bekezdés: megkérdezte, maradhatnak-e a méhek.

qs.q: The neighbour helped Amira by
opts: doing the most difficult jobs for her.
giving her new equipment.
advising her while she worked.
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: nem nyúlt semmihez, csak tanácsot adott („told me to slow down”).

qs.q: Amira is allowed to use the school’s land because she
opts: teaches the children about bees.
pays a small rent.
gives the school some of her honey.
qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: cserébe előadásokat tart a tanulóknak.

qs.q: What interests Amira most about bees?
opts: the money she earns from honey
the way the queen controls the others
how the group acts without a leader
qs.expl: 4. bekezdés: a királynő nem parancsol, „nobody is in charge”.

qs.q: Amira decided not to give up because
opts: the disease disappeared.
a child showed interest in her bees.
her neighbour gave her new colonies.
qs.expl: 5. bekezdés: egy hétéves gyerek üzenete miatt gondolta meg magát.

qs.q: When Amira goes to university, the hives will
opts: be cared for by young people who heard her talks.
be moved to another place.
be sold at the market.
qs.expl: 6. bekezdés: három korábbi hallgatója vállalta a gondozásukat.

p2.title: The return of the paper notebook
paras: A few years ago it seemed certain that paper was on its way out. Phones could store every appointment, shopping list and idea, and they never ran out of pages. (1) ______ In several countries, sales of notebooks and diaries have been rising steadily.

Part of the explanation lies in how memory works. When students type their notes, they tend to copy the teacher’s words exactly. (2) ______ This extra effort of choosing what to write appears to help the information stay in the mind.
There is also the question of attention. A phone that holds your to-do list holds a great many other things as well. (3) ______ A notebook, by contrast, can do only one thing.
For some people the attraction is simply physical. (4) ______ None of these small pleasures can be copied by a screen.

Of course, paper has obvious disadvantages. It cannot remind you of a meeting, and it cannot be searched. (5) ______ Many users therefore combine the two, keeping appointments on the phone and thoughts on paper.
Perhaps the real reason is that a notebook is private in a way that few things are today. (6) ______ What you write there is for you alone.
sents: Those who write by hand are slower, so they are forced to summarise.
They like the feel of good paper, the sound of a pen and the sight of a finished page.
Most schools have already replaced them with tablets.
And yet stationery shops are busier than they have been for a long time.
Nobody counts how often you open it, and nobody sends you advertisements based on what it contains.
If you lose it on a train, there is no copy.
You pick it up to check one task and, twenty minutes later, you are still looking at photographs.
expl: Az „And yet” ellentétet jelez: a papír mégsem tűnt el; utána a növekvő eladások következnek.
A gépelők és a kézzel írók szembeállítása; a „This extra effort” az összefoglalásra utal.
Az „it” a telefon, amely eltereli a figyelmet; ezzel áll szemben a füzet („by contrast”).
A „They” azokra utal, akiket a papír fizikai élménye vonz; a „these small pleasures” ezeket foglalja össze.
Újabb hátrány a felsorolásban: ha elveszik, nincs másolat.
A füzet magánjellegét fejti ki: senki sem figyeli, mit írsz bele.

texts: Gates open at noon on both days. Please note that glass bottles, umbrellas and professional cameras are not permitted inside the festival area. Drinking water is available next to the first-aid tent. The last shuttle bus to the railway station leaves at 12.30 a.m., half an hour after the final concert ends.

After last year’s mud and endless queues, I had promised myself never to return to Riverside Sounds. I am glad I broke that promise. The organisers have doubled the number of food stalls, the sound on the second stage was excellent, and the headline band played for two full hours. Only the ticket price still hurts.

Riverside Sounds needs sixty helpers for this summer’s festival. In return for two six-hour shifts, you will receive a free weekend ticket, meals and a place on the staff campsite. No experience is necessary, but you must be at least sixteen. Under-eighteens need written permission from a parent.

I have nothing against young people enjoying themselves, and I accept that the festival brings money into the town. But for three nights my family could not sleep before one o’clock, and on Monday our street was covered in rubbish. I would ask the organisers to end the music earlier and to pay for the cleaning.

p4.title: The message in the bottle
paras: In the summer of 1998 a nine-year-old girl called Lena Vogt was on a ferry crossing the North Sea with her parents. Bored after several hours on deck, she wrote a short letter, put it into an empty lemonade bottle and threw it over the side. The letter gave her name and address and asked the finder to write back. Then she forgot all about it.

The bottle was found twenty-one years later on a beach in northern Norway by a fisherman named Odd Larsen, who was collecting plastic rubbish with his grandchildren. The paper inside was damp but the pencil could still be read. Larsen, who spoke no German, asked the local teacher to translate it.

Finding Lena was not simple. The family had moved house twice, and a letter sent to the address in the bottle was returned unopened. It was the teacher’s idea to contact a newspaper in Lena’s home town. The paper printed a photograph of the letter, and within two days a former neighbour had recognised the name and telephoned Lena’s mother.

By then Lena was thirty and working as a nurse in Hamburg. She says that when her mother rang, she first thought it was a mistake, and only believed the story when she saw the picture of her own childish drawing of a ship at the bottom of the page.

The following spring she travelled to Norway to meet the Larsen family. She stayed for a week, went out on the fishing boat and was given the bottle as a present. In return she brought a new letter, written this time by her own daughter. The two families threw it into the sea together from the end of the harbour wall, and Larsen’s grandchildren have promised to write if it ever comes back.

qs.q: What kind of bottle did Lena use?
qs.expl: 1. bekezdés: egy üres limonádésüveget.

qs.q: How many years later was the bottle found?
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: huszonegy évvel később.

qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: „a fisherman named Odd Larsen”.

qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: egy volt szomszéd.

qs.expl: 4. bekezdés: ápolóként dolgozott Hamburgban.

qs.q: Who wrote the new letter?
qs.expl: 5. bekezdés: Lena lánya írta.

p1.title: A day as a film extra
paras: When a film company announced that it needed three hundred local people for a crowd scene, Jonas Petri sent in his photograph without telling anyone. Two weeks later the seventeen-year-old was standing in the main square of his own town at five in the morning, dressed as a factory worker from the 1930s.

He had imagined that the day would be exciting. In fact, most of it was spent waiting. The extras were given their costumes, had their hair cut in an old-fashioned style and were then told to sit in a cold sports hall until they were called. Jonas had brought nothing to read, and phones had to be handed in at the door so that no pictures of the set could appear online.

The scene itself lasted less than a minute on screen, but it took nine hours to film. The crowd had to run across the square again and again while the camera was moved, the light changed, or a modern road sign was discovered in the background. ‘By the twentieth time, nobody needed to act tired,’ Jonas says.

What impressed him was the attention to detail. A woman spent the whole day checking that none of the extras was wearing a watch. Another did nothing but pour water over the cobblestones so that they would look the same in every shot. ‘I had always thought films were made by the director and the stars,’ he says. ‘There were about two hundred people there whose names I will never know.’

The famous lead actor appeared for only an hour, and Jonas saw him from a distance of fifty metres. He was not disappointed. During the long wait he had got talking to one of the sound technicians, who let him listen through her headphones and explained what she was recording.

When the film finally reached the cinema, Jonas went with his whole family. He could not find himself in the crowd. It hardly mattered: he had already applied for a summer course in sound engineering.

qs.q: Jonas applied to be an extra
opts: together with some friends.
secretly.
because his family encouraged him.
qs.expl: 1. bekezdés: „without telling anyone”.

qs.q: What was most of the day like?
opts: It involved a lot of waiting.
It was as exciting as he had hoped.
It was spent learning to act.
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: „most of it was spent waiting”.

qs.q: Why did the extras have to give up their phones?
opts: Their costumes had no pockets.
The phones disturbed the sound recording.
The company wanted to stop photos being shared.
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: hogy ne kerülhessenek képek a díszletről az internetre.

qs.q: One reason the scene was repeated was that
opts: the extras kept making mistakes.
something from the wrong period was noticed.
the lead actor arrived late.
qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: egy modern közlekedési tábla került a háttérbe.

qs.q: What did Jonas learn about film-making?
opts: The director does most of the work.
It costs more than he had imagined.
It depends on many people who stay unknown.
qs.expl: 4. bekezdés: kétszáz ember dolgozott ott, akiknek a nevét sosem fogja megtudni.

qs.q: The most valuable part of the day for Jonas was
opts: meeting a member of the technical team.
seeing a famous actor.
appearing in the finished film.
qs.expl: 5–6. bekezdés: a hangtechnikussal beszélgetett, és jelentkezett egy hangmérnöki tanfolyamra.

p2.title: Repair cafés
paras: On the first Saturday of every month, the community hall in Elmfield fills with broken things. There are toasters that no longer toast, lamps that flicker and jeans with torn knees. (1) ______ They are volunteers, and they charge nothing for their time.
The rule of a repair café is that owners do not simply hand over an object and collect it later. (2) ______ The aim is that next time they will be able to do the job themselves.
Organisers say that about two thirds of the items brought in can be saved. (3) ______ A vacuum cleaner that seems dead may need nothing more than a new fuse costing a few cents.

Other cases are more frustrating. Many modern products are glued rather than screwed together, so they cannot be opened without being damaged. (4) ______ Campaigners are therefore asking for laws that would oblige companies to make their goods repairable.
The volunteers themselves are a mixed group. Some are retired engineers who miss using their skills. (5) ______ What they share is a dislike of waste and a certain pleasure in solving puzzles.
Visitors usually leave a small donation, which pays for the coffee and the hall. (6) ______ As one regular put it, she came for her radio and stayed for the conversation.
sents: Very often the fault turns out to be surprisingly small.
Others are teenagers who have taught themselves from online videos.
Behind a row of tables sit a dozen people with screwdrivers, needles and soldering irons.
The repair is normally finished within a week.
Spare parts are another problem, as manufacturers often refuse to sell them.
Many of them return the following month even when nothing they own is broken.
They sit beside the repairer and watch, or even hold the tools.
expl: A következő „They are volunteers” az asztaloknál ülő szerelőkre utal.
A tulajdonos nem adja le a tárgyat, hanem ott ül és figyel; ezért tudja majd legközelebb maga megcsinálni.
A hiba gyakran apró; a porszívó biztosítéka erre példa.
Az „another problem” a ragasztott termékek után újabb nehézséget említ: nincs alkatrész.
A „Some … Others” pár: nyugdíjas mérnökök és tizenévesek.
A „them” a látogatókra utal, akik visszajárnak; ezt erősíti a törzsvendég mondata.

texts: From 1 March the Northgate Pool will open one hour earlier on weekdays, at 6 a.m., following requests from members who swim before work. The small pool will be closed for repairs until the middle of April. During this period children’s lessons will take place in lanes one and two of the main pool.

Lakeside Leisure Centre requires two lifeguards for the summer season, June to August. Applicants must hold a current lifesaving certificate and be able to work at weekends. Full training in first aid will be provided. Send your CV to the manager by 15 May, giving the name of one person who can recommend you.

At forty-two I could not swim a single length, and I was too embarrassed to say so. My daughter finally persuaded me to join an adult beginners’ class. There were nine of us, all equally nervous. It took me four months to cross the pool without stopping. Last Sunday I swam in a lake for the first time in my life.

For serious swimmers, the Olympia Centre is hard to beat: fifty metres, eight lanes, and water kept at a sensible temperature. Families may prefer Splash World, which has slides and a wave machine but is noisy and far from cheap. Students should try the university pool, which costs half as much as either and is almost empty in the mornings.

p4.title: The mountain hut
paras: The Karlin Hut stands at 2,340 metres, three hours on foot from the nearest road. It was built in 1927 by a climbing club, and for most of a century it was run in the same way: a warden lived there from June to September, cooked simple meals and gave walkers a bed. Everything he needed was carried up by mule.

In 2016 the old warden retired, and the club could find nobody to replace him. The hut was closed for two summers. It was reopened by a couple in their twenties, Mira and Stefan Albrecht, who had met there as teenagers when they were both working as kitchen helpers.

They kept the wooden building as it was, but changed almost everything else. Electricity now comes from solar panels on the roof, and supplies arrive by helicopter four times each season, which is cheaper than keeping animals. Rainwater is collected in a tank behind the hut, so guests are asked to shower for no more than two minutes.

The Albrechts also introduced a rule that surprised many visitors: there is no wi-fi, and the couple have no intention of installing it. Instead, the dining room has a shelf of books and a collection of maps. Mira says that people complain on the first evening and thank her on the second.

Bookings have more than doubled. The hut’s forty beds are now full on most summer weekends, and reservations must be made online at least a week ahead. The work is hard – the day begins at five, when the first climbers want breakfast – and the season is short. In winter Stefan works as a ski instructor in the valley, while Mira writes the hut’s cookbook, which is to be published next year.

qs.q: Who built the hut?
qs.expl: 1. bekezdés: 1927-ben egy hegymászóklub építette.

qs.q: How were supplies carried up in the past?
qs.expl: 1. bekezdés: öszvérrel vittek fel mindent.

qs.q: How long was the hut closed?
qs.expl: 2. bekezdés: két nyáron át zárva volt.

qs.q: Where does the electricity come from?
qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: a tetőn lévő napelemekből.

qs.q: How long may guests shower?
qs.expl: 3. bekezdés: legfeljebb két percig.

qs.q: How many beds does the hut have?
qs.expl: 5. bekezdés: negyven ágy.

qs.q: What is Stefan’s job in winter?
qs.expl: 5. bekezdés: síoktató a völgyben.

writing.title: Email: language course
writing.task: You have seen an advertisement for a two-week summer English course in Dublin. Write an email to the course organiser. Say why you are interested in the course, ask about the accommodation and the price, and ask what you should bring with you.

writing.title: Email: a complaint
writing.task: Last week you bought a pair of headphones from an online shop, but they stopped working after two days. Write an email to the customer service manager. Explain what you bought and when, describe the problem, and say what you would like the company to do.

writing.title: Email: volunteering
writing.task: Your town library is looking for young volunteers to help at a children’s reading festival. Write an email to the librarian. Introduce yourself, explain why you would be a good volunteer, say when you are available, and ask one question about the event.

writing.title: Letter: a suggestion to the head teacher
writing.task: Your school is planning to spend some money on improving the building. Write a letter to the head teacher. Suggest one improvement, explain how students would benefit from it, and offer to help in some way.

writing.title: Letter to a friend: a new hobby
writing.task: Write a letter to an English-speaking friend about a hobby or sport you have recently started. Describe how you got into it, say what you enjoy most and what you find difficult, and invite your friend to try it with you.

writing.title: Article: the best day out
writing.task: Your school magazine has asked students to write about the best day out in their area. Write an article describing the place, explaining what people can do there, and saying why you would recommend it to visitors of your age.

writing.title: Story: an unexpected message
writing.task: Write a story for a student website which begins with this sentence: “When I looked at my phone that morning, I could not believe what I was reading.” Describe what the message said, what you did next, and how the day ended.

writing.title: Essay: learning online
writing.task: Write an essay for your class blog entitled “Is learning online as good as learning in a classroom?” Describe your own experience, give at least two advantages and two disadvantages, and finish with your own opinion.
